recipe.notes:
Serving: rcp-ndcg-vllm's folded model plugin (the one vllm.general_plugins entry point)
(rcp-ndcg-vllm/plugins/pplx/, pure Python, installed with pip install
--no-deps into the unmodified image) registers the checkpoint's
PplxContextualModel as a pooling model: the language_model.* weight mapper,
the contextual_projection head, and a chunk pooler that segments on the
boundary id 248079 and applies the int8 tanh head. It also registers the
checkpoint's transformers config class (hf_config.PplxContextualConfig, the
remote configuration class restated field for field), so --trust-remote-code
is unnecessary and the remote config module never executes. The plugin must
NOT register a multimodal processor (the ColQwen3_5 precedent it is modelled
on does): the embedding code is text-only, and a copy-paste would silently
embed images into a text model instead of rejecting them.

The wire contract (request_shape: token_ids). The reference tokenizes the
document with split_special_tokens=True, so the reference's document ids open
with the two literal tokens that the "[D] " string renders under that parse
(ids 62724, 60) while a server-side parse of the same text keeps the added
special id 248078 (measured at the pinned revision: 27 vs 26 tokens, divergence
at index 0); the boundary marker is a NON-special added token and keeps its one
id 248079 in both parses. The plugin implements the reference's id space and
refuses inputs whose first id is neither 248077 (the query prefix) nor
(62724, 60): queries are [248077] + tokenize(query); documents are the split
render of "[D] " + chunks joined by the boundary marker, with 248079 markers
and the prefix and markers excluded from every pooled span.

PRODUCT GAP (reported, not worked around): the product's token-ids route
tokenises the fitted render with the tokenizer's ADDED-TOKEN parse, which
opens a document with the one special id 248078 where the reference's
document ids open with (62724, 60) -- and the two parses' first content
pretoken differs as well (the measured 0..+2-token prefix delta). Queries
match the reference ids over that route (measured: [248077] + body equals the
remote's prepend construction). Documents therefore diverge at the prefix
boundary and the plugin REFUSES them loudly, so stage 2 can verify the query
leg today and cannot verify documents until the product's id derivation can
request the reference's split parse (a tokenizer parse mode on the ids path
-- transformers' split_special_tokens is the raw tokenizers
encode_special_tokens toggle -- consumed by the pooling client's token-id
derivation). Token ids stay the declared wire: it is the only route that can
carry the reference ids at all. The declared render TEXT is byte-identical to
the reference's on both shapes (stage 1 proves it), so the id-derivation seam
is the whole remaining delta.

Role disambiguation on the engine (the plugin's rule): first id 248077 -> query, pooled as the mean over
the whole sequence with the prefix token included; leading (62724, 60) ->
document, pooled as one span mean per chunk between 248079 markers, the
prefix and the markers excluded from every span. A one-chunk document has no
marker and is a single span; the leading id is the only role signal. An empty
chunk (consecutive or trailing markers) pools to the zero vector, the
reference's own branch for a chunk with no tokens.

Chunks: the document content is the model's chunk list joined by the boundary
marker - chunk boundaries are input to this model, and the chunker that
produces them is declared preprocessing recorded upstream of this recipe. A
chunk's text must contain no all-special token of this tokenizer; the
boundary marker is the declared case (the plugin segments on every 248079, so
a marker inside chunk text would create phantom chunks), and the reference's split-side parse makes
any other all-special token in content diverge from the engine-side parse the
same way. reference.py re-splits the content on the marker for the model call.

Scores: the card gives per-chunk scores (doc_embeddings @ query_embeddings)
but no aggregation; the product's multi-vector scorer (MaxSim with a single
query vector) pools by max over chunks. Max is the retrieval reading and
INFERENCE - the GPU wave confirms it against the vendor's retrieval numbers.

dtype: vLLM v0.31.0 cannot run this model in float32: the GDN prefill kernels
refuse it on every backend (flashinfer's _cutlass_io_dtype raises
"Unsupported dtype torch.float32, expected bfloat16 or float16", observed both at
kernel warmup and on the first forward when the checkpoint was served in float32 on
the stock v0.31.0 image; the Triton/FLA path
asserts "ChunkGatedDeltaRuleFunction does not support float32. Please use
bfloat16.", third_party/flash_linear_attention/ops/chunk.py:213-215 at the
tag). The recipe therefore serves dtype: bfloat16 (16.8 GB of weights; the
33,604,334,528-byte fp32 checkpoint is cast at load) while the REFERENCE
runs the checkpoint's own fp32 (the card's AutoModel.from_pretrained passes
no dtype, so the config's float32 loads) -- the served-vs-reference difference is the
cast plus the kernels, and stage 2's tolerance gate and the wave's retrieval
numbers quantify it. The first equivalence plan's float32 rung is deleted:
it is unservable on this engine. The int8 head stays fp32 on both sides (the
remote code's _keep_in_fp32_modules; the plugin's head_dtype). Skipping the
unused vision tower saves 1.82 GB fp32 (parsed from the checkpoint's shard
headers).

Budget: the model's own limit is 262144 tokens model-side (config
query_length and document_length; the model raises beyond it and truncates
nothing). The model-side count of a render is the engine-side count plus a
content-dependent prefix delta: the [D] prefix contributes +1 (two literal
ids where the engine-side count keeps one special id) minus whatever the
first content pretoken saves by re-tokenizing with the prefix's trailing
space - measured total deltas 0..+2 over letter, digit, whitespace, CJK and
emoji-initial content, worst 2. The client budget is therefore
262142: the measured worst case reserved, so no measured render hits the
model's own raise, and a content class outside the measured ones fails
loudly at the engine's own max_model_len, never silently. The pooling role
client fits every request to the declared tokenizer and budget before it
derives the token ids (rcp-ndcg/src/rcp_ndcg/inference/clients/pool.py: content-only
cuts, every cut census-recorded): the cut is the declared policy. The model card
has no over-limit output to compare with (it raises), so the pairs files keep
every text under the limit; reference.py's render of such a row is the uncut
prompt, which stage 1 reports as a mismatch. max_model_len
262144 reserves whole-sequence prefill (bidirectional pooling disables
chunked prefill at the pinned engine): roughly 8.5 GB of bf16 KV per 262k
sequence (the GDN state cache stays fp32 via mamba_ssm_dtype, small beside
it). The wave confirms the VRAM plan and lowers BOTH numbers deliberately,
never one, if the slot cannot afford the worst case.

Template file: no serve.chat_template. The /pooling completion route applies
no chat template at the pinned engine (pooling/protocol.py, io_processor.py),
the repo's chat_template.jinja is a chat-generation template containing none
of the embedding prefixes, and a served template file would be inert on this
route while the harness's template check renders one string that cannot equal
two declared shapes' different frames. The declared shapes above are the
frame the client tokenizes and sends as ids.

add_special_tokens: true declares the pooling route's engine default; this
tokenizer's post-processor appends nothing (bos is null, measured), so the
reserved block is empty and the ids are identical either way.

Template segments: the two role prefixes are written by NAME
({special:[Q] } / {special:[D] }): the product's special-name resolution
keeps a name's significant whitespace exactly, and these added
tokens' names carry a significant trailing space. The render check against
the reference's constants pins the resolved spelling.

MRL {1024, 2048} is NOT declared (dimensions and mrl_dim unset): the card's
cut takes the first 1024 of the UNNORMALISED values and renormalises, and the
product's client-side mrl_dim now implements exactly that
cut-then-renormalise -- adopting MRL is one field away when the wave wants
the 1024-dim run. normalize: true matches the card's usage
(normalize_embeddings); the plugin's request-level activation L2-normalises
by default and the end state matches either way. empty_doc: send exercises
the model's own empty-chunk branch (the zero vector) instead of substituting
a product-side zero; the wave should confirm the plugin reproduces it - and
name the one divergence between the plugin and the remote code: the remote code RAISES for a non-empty chunk that yields no tokens, the
plugin zero-pools it, unreachable under this recipe's declared chunker
guarantee for this tokenizer. pad_token is the tokenizer's endoftext token
and there is no bos token (tokenizer_config.json). The card states no
chunking policy of its own: chunk boundaries are model input, and the
chunker's guarantee - no all-special token inside chunk text, the boundary
marker being the declared case - is declared here.
